# Advent of Code

My [Advent of Code](https://adventofcode.com) solutions, several languages and
years, each built and run in a pinned toolchain container so that compiler and
runtime updates never break old solutions.

Verified by CI against my puzzle inputs; see [Continuous integration](#continuous-integration).

## Layout

```
<year>/<impl>/aoc.toml     how this implementation is built and run (see below)
<year>/<impl>/...          the solutions
tools/aoc/                 the `aoc` CLI (Rust)
results.json               verified status per solution (written by CI; no answers)
```

An implementation is any directory `<year>/<impl>/` with an `aoc.toml`. The
directory name is its id, so a year can have several (`rust`, `rust-simd`,
`haskell`, ...).

### The solution contract

* The puzzle input arrives on **stdin**. `AOC_YEAR`, `AOC_DAY` and `AOC_PART`
  are also set.
* The answer is the **last non-empty line of stdout**, so debug output printed
  before it is fine. stderr is free-form.
* Exit with status 0.
* Runs have **no network access**, read-only source, and a timeout (60s by default).

### `aoc.toml`

```toml
language = "rust"
# The toolchain, pinned by digest (`cargo aoc toolchain pin 2025/rust` fills it in)...
image = "docker.io/library/rust:1.91.1-slim@sha256:..."
# ...or built from a Dockerfile in this directory: dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

# Which solutions exist. Placeholders: {day} = 7, {dd} = 07, {part} = 1 or 2.
# Without {part}, each day has both parts. A trailing / matches directories.
discover = "{dd}/part{part}/Cargo.toml"
# ...or list them: days = [1, 2, 3]

# Commands run with `sh -c` in the container, in this directory (mounted at
# /src). {cache} is a per-implementation directory that persists between runs.
# Builds may use the network; a build without {day}/{dd}/{part} runs once.
build = "cargo install --locked --path {dd}/part{part} --root {cache}/out/{dd}-{part}"
run = "{cache}/out/{dd}-{part}/bin/*"

sources = "{dd}/part{part}"   # files that make up one solution (cache keys); default: everything
timeout = "60s"
# platform = "linux/amd64"    # if the image has no build for your machine

[env]
CARGO_HOME = "{cache}/cargo-home"

[day.12]                       # per-day overrides
timeout = "5m"
# parts = [1]                  # when `discover` has no {part}

[new]                          # how `cargo aoc new` scaffolds a solution (optional)
template = "template"          # copied in first (see below)
command = "cargo init --vcs none --name part{part} {dd}/part{part}"  # then run like `build`
```

### Scaffolding: `[new]`

`cargo aoc new YEAR DAY [PART]` creates a solution from the implementation's `[new]` section:

1. **`template`** names a folder that mirrors the implementation's layout. Its
   files are copied in, with `{{year}} {{day}} {{dd}} {{part}}` expanded in both
   file names and contents. The double braces keep code like Rust's
   `println!("{day}")` or Python's `f"{day}"` intact. A Python implementation
   whose `discover` is `{dd}/{part}.py` needs just one file:
   `template/{{dd}}/{{part}}.py`.
2. **`command`** (optional) then runs exactly like `build`: in the
   implementation's pinned toolchain container, with network access and the
   `{day} {dd} {part}` placeholders. Use it for anything a file copy can't do.
   The Rust implementations copy `template/{{dd}}/part{{part}}/src/main.rs`,
   then run `cargo init` and `cargo generate-lockfile`. Because the pinned `cargo`
   does this, the edition and lockfile format always suit that toolchain.

`new` never overwrites anything. If the command fails, everything it created is
removed, so you can fix the problem and re-run. Templates belong to an
implementation because they depend on its toolchain. For example, Bun 1.0.15's
`Bun.stdin.text()` fails on piped input, so the 2023 template avoids it. When
you start a new implementation, copy the previous one's `aoc.toml` and
`template/` and adjust them.

Implementations without `[new]`, such as the 2021/2022 Haskell projects (each new
day also has to be registered in `Main.hs`), are set up by hand.

Upgrading a toolchain is a deliberate edit to one implementation's manifest;
nothing else moves. Start a new year (or a new compiler version) by adding a new
implementation with a new image.

## The `aoc` CLI

Needs Docker (or Podman: `AOC_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman`) and Rust. `cargo aoc`
is an alias (`.cargo/config.toml`) that compiles the CLI on first use and
incrementally after that, so it works from anywhere in the repository.

```sh
cargo aoc list                       # implementations and their solutions
cargo aoc new 2025 8                 # scaffold day 8 part 1 from the [new] template
cargo aoc new 2025 8 2               # ...and part 2 (--impl ID if the year has several)
cargo aoc test 2025/7                # build, run and check day 7 (all implementations)
cargo aoc test 2025 --impl rust      # one implementation
cargo aoc test 2025/7/2 --examples   # against the examples instead of the real input
cargo aoc run 2025 7 1               # print the answer (checks it if one is recorded)
cargo aoc run 2025 7 1 --input -     # ...on input from stdin
cargo aoc run 2025 7 1 --native      # use the host toolchain: fast, not reproducible
cargo aoc build --since main         # build implementations changed since a git ref
cargo aoc fetch 2025 7               # download input + your submitted answers
cargo aoc readme                     # rebuild the progress table from results.json
cargo aoc toolchain pin 2025/rust    # resolve an image tag to a digest
cargo aoc doctor                     # check the setup
```

Selectors are `YEAR`, `YEAR/DAY` or `YEAR/DAY/PART`. Run `cargo aoc help <command>`
for all options.

## Workflow

**New implementation** (a language in a year):

1. Create `<year>/<name>/aoc.toml`. The easiest way is to copy the previous one
   in that language, along with its `template/`. Set `image` to a plain tag,
   such as `docker.io/library/rust:1.97.0-slim`.
2. Run `cargo aoc toolchain pin <year>/<name>` to record the image's digest.
3. Commit. `cargo aoc list` shows the new implementation with no days yet. Years
   from 2025 on have 12 days.

**New day:**

1. `cargo aoc fetch 2026 8` downloads the input into the data repository (once the puzzle unlocks).
2. `cargo aoc new 2026 8` scaffolds part 1, with the stdin boilerplate already written.
3. Iterate. `cargo aoc run 2026 8 1 --native` is fast. `cargo aoc test 2026/8/1`
   uses the pinned container, and prints `output: ...` until an answer is recorded.
4. Submit the answer on adventofcode.com, then run `cargo aoc fetch 2026 8` again
   to record it. Do the same for part 2, starting with `cargo aoc new 2026 8 2`.

**Test cases:** example inputs come from the puzzle text, so they live in the
data repository as well. Add `2026/08/1.txt` and an `examples.toml` with the
expected answers (see [Puzzle data](#puzzle-data)), then run
`cargo aoc test 2026/8 --examples`. Use `--input FILE` (or `-` for stdin) with
`cargo aoc run` for one-off inputs.

**Pushing:**

1. Commit and push the data repository first: the input, `answers.toml` and any examples.
2. Commit the solution (for Rust, its `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `src/`) and
   push to `main`. A pull request from a branch is also checked against your
   data, but only `main` updates the README.
3. CI verifies the changed solutions and commits the progress table. Run
   `git pull --rebase` before you next push. If the data arrived after the
   solution, re-run the workflow from the Actions tab.

## Puzzle data

Puzzle inputs and answers are copyrighted and must not be published, so they
live in a separate **private** repository, laid out as:

```
<year>/<dd>/input.txt
<year>/<dd>/answers.toml     part1 = "1234"  part2 = "5678"
<year>/<dd>/examples.toml    [[example]]  input = "1.txt"  part1 = "..."   (optional)
<year>/<dd>/1.txt            example inputs (optional)
```

For "read the letters off the ASCII art" puzzles, use `part2_output = """..."""`
in `answers.toml` to compare the full output instead.

Clone it to `.aoc-data/` (gitignored) or point `AOC_DATA_DIR` at it. Settings
can also go in a gitignored `.env` file at the repository root:

```sh
AOC_DATA_DIR=~/src/AdventOfCode-data
AOC_SESSION=...           # the `session` cookie from adventofcode.com, for `fetch`
AOC_USER_AGENT="github.com/DanielPower/AdventOfCode by you@example.com"
```

`cargo aoc fetch YEAR [DAY]` downloads inputs and scrapes the answers you have
already submitted from the puzzle pages. It skips files that exist and waits
between requests. Commit the results to the data repository.
`cargo aoc data import` moves files from the old layout (`<year>/data/DD.in`,
`DD.P.out`) into the data directory.

## Continuous integration

`.github/workflows/verify.yml` runs on pushes to `main`, on pull requests,
weekly, and on demand:

1. It checks out the private data repository with a read-only deploy key.
2. `aoc test --ci --save --changed` builds and runs every solution whose source,
   manifest, toolchain or data changed since the last recorded result. The weekly
   run re-verifies everything to prove old toolchains still work.
3. It regenerates the progress table and commits `README.md` and `results.json`.

`--ci` never prints answers, solution output or solution stderr (build errors
are shown; they contain code, not input), and masks every answer in the log.
Pull requests from forks get no secrets, so they only build.

One-time setup:

1. Create a private repository, e.g. `AdventOfCode-data`, with the layout above.
2. `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f aoc-data-key -N ""`. Add `aoc-data-key.pub` as a
   **read-only deploy key** on the data repository, and the private key as the
   secret `AOC_DATA_DEPLOY_KEY` on this one.
3. If the data repository isn't named `<this repo>-data`, set the Actions
   variable `AOC_DATA_REPO` to `owner/name`.
4. Optional: set the variable `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` and the secret `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`
   (a read-only access token) to avoid Docker Hub's anonymous pull limits.
5. If `main` is protected, allow GitHub Actions to push to it.
